sentences.text: On the Brindle-Voice test set, Brisling achieved a WER of 6.4% with a median latency of 41 ms per utterance, compared to Talmar's WER of 6.1% and median latency of 118 ms.
Brisling required 4.0 decoder passes per utterance, whereas Talmar required 37.6 passes, indicating a substantial reduction in decoding steps.

Although Brisling's WER was 0.3 percentage points higher than Talmar's, it achieved a 65% reduction in median latency, and no statistical test was reported to assess the significance of the WER difference.
